projects.name: WGS Extract
projects.progress: Releasing regularly (v0.8.x). The desktop app is in alpha, and Linux ARM64 support is in phase 1.
projects.summary: A local-first toolkit that turns whole-genome sequencing files into useful files, reports and extracts, as a scriptable CLI plus a desktop app.
highlights: An independent command-line rewrite of WGS Extract that wraps samtools, bcftools, bwa/minimap2, GATK, Haplogrep and VEP
Inspects BAM/CRAM files, simulates consumer microarray files (23andMe, AncestryDNA), and calls and annotates variants
Includes native Yleaf-derived Y-DNA haplogroup analysis
Ships a cross-platform desktop app (Tauri) built with GUI for CLI, plus one-line installers
Built to be AI-agent friendly: everything is a CLI command with structured output

projects.name: GUI for CLI
projects.progress: Folded into WGS Extract as a single Tauri app. The ~30-toolkit experiments live on the old-experimental branch; see the AI desktop UI evaluation.
projects.summary: Turns a portable CLI-tool bundle into an installable desktop app. It started as the testbed for my AI desktop UI evaluation and became the framework behind the WGS Extract desktop app.
highlights: One TypeScript app: a web UI and a local Node backend, packaged as a native app with Tauri
Data-driven pages: setup steps, long-running commands, dynamic data sources, localisation, file pickers and terminal output
Served as the shared app for the AI desktop UI evaluation across about 30 toolkits
Over 600 commits and 22 releases before it was folded into WGS Extract

screenshots.caption: Running the WGS Extract example bundle

projects.name: AI desktop UI evaluation: one app, ~30 toolkits
projects.progress: Ran 7–26 May 2026 with GPT-5.5 in GitHub Copilot CLI (plus GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.7). The rewrites averaged 2.55/5; SwiftUI and Tauri won, and Tauri now ships in WGS Extract.
projects.summary: I had AI agents build the same real desktop app in about 30 UI toolkits, then benchmarked every window and hand-rated every screenshot to see how well each one came out.
highlights: SwiftUI, AppKit, Tauri, Electron, Flutter, Compose, Slint, Gio, Iced, egui, ImGui, Raygui, Qt/QML, GTK4, Avalonia, wxPython, Textual and more, all running the WGS Extract bundle
34 screenshots rated 1–5, with implementation difficulty, completeness and active hours per toolkit
The fastest renderers (4–21 ms) were rated 2/5; Flutter, Compose Desktop, wxPython and Swift AppKit reached 4/5
Reusing one complete WebUI beat rewriting the app per toolkit; the WebUI launchers mostly tested packaging, startup and memory

screenshots.caption: Slint: rated 2/5 despite an excellent footprint
C++ Dear ImGui: fastest (3.6 ms), rated 2/5
Avalonia: rated 1/5 (a config error on screen)

projects.name: Apple Silicon aligner hillclimb
projects.progress: Ran 4–10 November 2026, mostly with Claude Opus 5.5 in GitHub Copilot CLI. 14 prereleases in six days; WGS Extract picks these builds automatically when they're installed on a Mac.
projects.summary: AI agents rebuilt BWA, BWA-MEM2, bwa-mem3 and minimap2 for Apple Silicon and Metal one measured step at a time, keeping byte-identical alignments: BWA ran 3.9× faster at half the energy.
highlights: wgse-bwa --metal: 528.5 s → 125.9 s on 5M human read pairs, climbing version by version from GPU seeding to mate rescue, extension and overlap
Exact CPU-only rewrites too: BWA −53% and BWA-MEM2 −44% (with a third less memory) using interleaved walks and NEON
minimap2 up to −44% (multi-threaded index building), with --metal gap fills on the GPU for long reads
Energy measured with powermetrics: --metal halves the Wh per genome
A whole 35x genome from BAM to report in 7.3 hours on a base 16 GB M1

screenshots.caption: A base 16 GB M1: CPU vs Metal

projects.name: The Dawn-Breakers
projects.progress: 21 chapters are built, so every part of Nabíl's narrative now has a place in the game: 65 maps, from Karbilá in 1843 to the Black Pit of Ṭihrán in 1853. It also has mini-games, journeys, a map editor, and English, Persian and Chinese text.
projects.summary: A 2.5D isometric web RPG that follows Nabíl's narrative The Dawn-Breakers through 21 chapters. You explore historical places, talk to people and follow the story.
highlights: 21 chapters, from the Forerunners in Karbilá (1843) through Shíráz, Mecca, Badasht, Ṭabarsí, Nayríz and Zanján, to the Black Pit of Ṭihrán (1852–53)
Isometric exploration, reflective dialogue, a journal with objectives, and chapter progression with saves

Journeys between chapters: each road plays out under the true night sky for its date and place (real Hipparcos stars, the moon in its phase, twilight), with the days rolling by until dawn at the arrival
Mini-games and a built-in map editor
Animated sunrise title screen with its own soundtrack; English, Persian and Chinese text
Most of the code, art, music, writing and translation was made with AI, and the game says so

screenshots.caption: The sunrise title card, just after the sun clears the horizon

Karbilá: the palm groves on the canal

projects.name: Amaran Light CLI
projects.progress: Published on npm as amaran-light-cli with 25 releases. A Raspberry Pi runs the daemon, dashboard and circadian service for my desk lights every day.
projects.summary: Controls Aputure Amaran lights from the command line or a local web dashboard, through Amaran Desktop or directly over Bluetooth Mesh, with circadian lighting that follows the sun.
highlights: A local control dashboard: live per-light readback with estimated lux, brightness/lux/Kelvin sliders, and colour, effects, fan and group controls
auto-cct sets colour temperature and brightness from the sun's position, with live-weather adjustment and a daily Kelvin/intensity/lux graph
A background service applies it every minute, with per-light caps and temporary manual overrides
Its own Bluetooth Mesh daemon, so the vendor app is optional; runs on macOS or Linux (systemd)
Presets, scenes, groups, effects, fan profiles and thermal telemetry from the CLI too

screenshots.caption: Dashboard: live light status and the circadian schedule (location hidden)
Dashboard: power, white light, colour, effects and fan controls

projects.name: Reddit ZST to Parquet
projects.progress: Converted my full multi-terabyte Reddit archive (comments and submissions up to 2026-03). It still has rough edges.
projects.summary: Converts huge Reddit Zstandard dumps into analytical Parquet files, using several machines that coordinate through your NAS.
highlights: Distributed by design: workers on different machines claim work through a ticket system on shared storage
Tunes DuckDB memory and threads to each machine
Resilient transfers over FTP/FTPS, rsync/SSH, NFS or local disks
Writes a JSON manifest with row counts and column stats for every Parquet file

projects.name: Email Sorter
projects.progress: Used on my own gigabytes of mail. You bring your own local LLM server.
projects.summary: An offline email classification pipeline that sorts gigabytes of mail with heuristics and local language models, spread across several LLM machines.
highlights: Ingests Google Takeout mbox files or Fastmail through JMAP
Runs fast heuristics and language detection first, then sends the rest to an LLM
Works with any OpenAI-compatible server (LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM), and with several machines at once
Exports ban and unsubscribe lists, with a browser-based unsubscribe fallback
